          "statement": "Input an exact rational $q$, an exact rational target $0<\\tau\\le1/4$, integer dyadic exponent limits $e_{\\min}\\le e_{\\max}$, an initial precision $p_0\\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\\max}\\ge p_0$, and a finite elementary-series cap $J\\ge1$. The target value is $w=e^{\\pi iq}=\\cos(\\pi q)+i\\sin(\\pi q)$ by [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], for the canonical Fourier $\\pi$ identified with the interval evaluator's constant by [[thm-na-interval-pi-matches-canonical-fourier-pi]]. For each precision $p=p_0,p_0+1,\\ldots,p_{\\max}$, and $t\\in\\{1/5,1/239\\}$, form the exact rational interval $I_J(t)=[A_J(t)-R_J(t),A_J(t)+R_J(t)]$, where\n$$A_J(t)=\\sum_{j=0}^{J}\\frac{(-1)^jt^{2j+1}}{2j+1},\\qquad R_J(t)=\\frac{|t|^{2J+3}}{(2J+3)(1-t^2)}.$$\nThe Machin identity gives the interval $P=16I_J(1/5)-4I_J(1/239)$ containing $\\pi$. Form the exact rational interval $qP$ by taking the minimum and maximum of its two endpoint products, then round its endpoints down and up to obtain a dyadic input interval $\\Theta$ in format $(p,e_{\\min},e_{\\max})$. If this conversion overflows, treat that precision as a non-finite evaluation. Otherwise build two finite real expression DAGs with input interval $\\Theta$ and requested outputs $\\cos(\\Theta)$ and $\\sin(\\Theta)$, and call [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] using the same dyadic format and truncation index $J$; its fixed finite-cell rules govern range reduction. If either result is non-finite, continue at the next precision unless the precision cap is reached, in which case return `inconclusive` with the supplier status. If the results are finite intervals $C=[c_-,c_+]$ and $S=[s_-,s_+]$, set $\\widehat w=c_-+is_-$ and compute an upward-rounded dyadic $\\epsilon\\ge(c_+-c_-)+(s_+-s_-)$. If $\\epsilon\\le\\tau$, return `certified(\\widehat w,\\epsilon)`; otherwise continue or return `inconclusive` at the cap. A non-finite endpoint or overflow returns its explicit failure status. The routine makes no finite-error claim on a failure branch.\n\n"

          "statement": "Input a real or complex matrix $A\\in\\mathbb F^{m\\times n}$ with $m\\ge n$, a target $k$ with $0\\le k<n$, a factor $f\\ge1$, and a finite swap cap $S\\in\\mathbb N\\cup\\{0\\}$. Otherwise initialize a column permutation $\\Pi$ and the full column-pivoted QR factorization $A\\Pi=QR$, where $Q\\in\\mathbb F^{m\\times m}$ is unitary and $R\\in\\mathbb F^{m\\times n}$ is upper trapezoidal. At each pivot choose a remaining column of maximal residual $2$-norm, resolving ties by the smallest original column index. Partition $R=\\begin{bmatrix}R_{11}&R_{12}\\\\0&R_{22}\\end{bmatrix}$ after the first $k$ rows and columns. Do not return the reduced QR form. The selected first $k$ columns then have a nonsingular leading block. For $k=0$, return this full factorization with `success`.\n2. For $k>0$, refactor the current fixed column order in the full QR form, without further pivoting whenever needed, using unitary Householder or Givens transformations. For $1\\le i\\le k$ let $\\omega_i=\\|e_i^*R_{11}^{-1}\\|_2$; for $1\\le j\\le n-k$ let $\\gamma_j=\\|R_{22}(:,j)\\|_2$. Define the swap score $s_{ij}=\\bigl(|X_{ij}|^2+(\\omega_i\\gamma_j)^2\\bigr)^{1/2}$.\n4. If $\\max_{i,j}|X_{ij}|>f$, choose the lexicographically first pair attaining the largest $|X_{ij}|$. Otherwise, if $\\max_{i,j}s_{ij}>f$, choose the lexicographically first pair attaining the largest score. If neither inequality holds, return `success` and the factors, permutation, $X$, and maximum score. When a violating pair was chosen, if the swap count is already $S$, return `swap-budget-exhausted` with the current partial factors. Write the diagonal as $d_i$ and superdiagonal as $e_i$, and set $e_0=0$.\n\nAt the start of each pass, set $t\\leftarrow t+1$, set $e_i$ to zero and append $(t,i,e_i^{old})$ to the deflation record whenever $|e_i|\\le\\tau(|d_i|+|d_{i+1}|)$.           "title": "Compact spectral filters, source conditions, and qualification",
          "statement": "Assume Countable Choice. Let $X,Y$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces and let\n$A:X\\to Y$ be compact and bounded. Put $S=A^*A$. By\n[[lem-compact-gram-operator-is-positive-and-has-kernel]], $S$ is compact,\npositive, and self-adjoint, with $\\ker S=\\ker A$. Let $\\Sigma$ be the set of\nnonzero eigenvalues of $S$ and $P_t$ the orthogonal projection onto the\neigenspace of $t\\in\\Sigma$; let $P_0$ be the orthogonal projection onto\n$\\ker S$. The compact spectral multiplier of a bounded scalar function\n$q:\\{0\\}\\cup\\Sigma\\to\\mathbb F$ is\n$$q(S)x:=q(0)P_0x+\\sum_{t\\in\\Sigma}q(t)P_tx,$$\nwhere the finite-subset net converges in norm by\n[[lem-compact-spectral-multiplier-is-well-defined]]. For $\\nu>0$, define\n$S^\\nu$ by the multiplier $q_\\nu(0)=0$ and $q_\\nu(t)=t^\\nu$ for $t>0$.\nThis multiplier is bounded: if $t\\in\\Sigma$ and $u\\in E_t$ is a unit vector,\nthen $0<t=\\|Su\\|\\le\\|S\\|$, so $|q_\\nu(t)|\\le\\|S\\|^\\nu$.\n\nFor $\\lambda>0$, the Tikhonov filter and residual filter are\n$$g_\\lambda(t)=\\frac1{t+\\lambda},\\qquad r_\\lambda(t)=1-tg_\\lambda(t)=\\frac{\\lambda}{t+\\lambda}.$$\nThe Tikhonov solution for data $y_\\delta\\in Y$ is\n$$x_\\lambda^\\delta=g_\\lambda(S)A^*y_\\delta =(A^*A+\\lambda I_X)^{-1}A^*y_\\delta.$$\nIndeed, the spectral decomposition gives $S+\\lambda I_X$ the multiplier\n$t+\\lambda$ on each $E_t$ and $\\lambda$ on $\\ker S$, so $g_\\lambda(S)$ is\nits inverse, whose existence is also supplied by\n[[lem-hilbert-tikhonov-normal-operator-invertible]].\nThe source condition of order $\\nu>0$ and radius $R\\ge0$ means that\n$x^\\dagger=S^\\nu w$ for some $w\\in X$ with $\\|w\\|\\le R$. A family of\nfilters $g_\\alpha$ with residual filters $r_\\alpha(t)=1-tg_\\alpha(t)$ has\nqualification at least $p>0$ when, for each $0<\\nu\\le p$, some finite\nconstant $C_\\nu\\ge0$ satisfies\n$$t^\\nu|r_\\alpha(t)|\\le C_\\nu\\alpha^\\nu \\quad\\text{for every }\\alpha>0\\text{ and }t\\in\\Sigma.$$\nWhen $\\Sigma=\\varnothing$, this condition is vacuous.\n\n"

          "statement": "Let $A$ be the input, set $\\widehat H_0=A$, and include every Hessenberg and QR update and every pure deflation write among stages $j=1,\\ldots,m$. The finite reduction's represented product is $Q=P_1\\cdots P_m$ (with $P_j=I$ for a pure deflation stage), and its final matrix is $\\widehat T=\\widehat H_m$, after any finite successful prefix or completed run. Suppose\n$$\\widehat H_j=P_j^*(\\widehat H_{j-1}+E_j+D_j)P_j,\\qquad \\|E_j\\|_F\\le\\alpha_j\\|\\widehat H_{j-1}\\|_F,$$\nwhere $D_j$ is the signed additive change from exact deflation zero writes (zero minus each overwritten value) and each $P_j$ is the exact stored-vector representative. Then\n$$\\widehat T=Q^*(A+\\Delta)Q,\\qquad \\|\\Delta\\|_F\\le\\sum_j\\alpha_j\\|\\widehat H_{j-1}\\|_F+\\sum_j\\|D_j\\|_F.$$\nThe conditional assertion holds for any certified nonnegative $\\alpha_j$. It covers initialization as well as all chase steps. Identity branches have zero arithmetic error. Deflation remains separate.\n\nIf the finite reduction returns certificate status certified and accumulator $C_{\\rm acc}$, then also\n$$\\sum_j\\alpha_j\\|\\widehat H_{j-1}\\|_F+\\sum_j\\|D_j\\|_F\\le C_{\\rm acc},$$\nso $C_{\\rm acc}$ is a reported upper bound for $\\|\\Delta\\|_F$.           "kind": "lemma",
          "title": "A scaled Chebyshev polynomial suppresses a separated interval",
          "statement": "Let $a>b>c$ be real numbers, let $k\\in\\mathbb N$ with $k\\ge0$, and put\n\n$$\\xi(x):=\\frac{2x-b-c}{b-c},\\qquad \\xi_a:=\\xi(a)=1+\\frac{2(a-b)}{b-c}>1.$$\n\nDefine\n\n$$p_k(x):=\\frac{T_k(\\xi(x))}{T_k(\\xi_a)},$$\n\nwhere $T_k$ is the $k$th Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind from\n[[def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind]]. Then $p_k$ is a real\npolynomial of degree exactly $k$, $p_k(a)=1$, and\n\n$$\\max_{x\\in[c,b]}|p_k(x)|=\\frac{1}{T_k(\\xi_a)}.$$\n\n",

          "kind": "proposition",
          "title": "Unrestarted GMRES has a sparse matvec plus orthogonalization work bound",
          "statement": "Let $A\\in\\mathbb R^{n\\times n}$ have a canonical CSR representation, with\n$n\\ge1$, at least one stored entry in every row, and\n$s=\\operatorname{nnz}(A)$. Let $r_0=b-Ax_0\\ne0$ and $1\\le m\\le n$. Run\nunrestarted GMRES in exact arithmetic for at most $m$ Arnoldi columns. At\ncolumn $j$, compute one CSR matrix-vector product, orthogonalize against the\n$j$ existing vectors by either one or two complete modified Gram–Schmidt\npasses, and update the projected least-squares problem by applying prior\nGivens rotations and forming one new rotation. Each Givens rotation is an\northogonal $2\\times2$ matrix on adjacent rows chosen to zero the current\nsubdiagonal entry. If Arnoldi completes $m$\ncolumns without breakdown, solve the resulting upper-triangular least-squares\nfactor; if it breaks down earlier, stop at that column and make no claim about\na separate rank-deficient fallback solve. Count field arithmetic and index\nwork, and exclude the stored input matrix. The total work in the no-breakdown\nbranch is $O(ms+m^2n)$ and the Krylov working storage is $O(mn)$. The same\nbounds cover all matvec, orthogonalization, and projected-rotation work\nactually performed before an earlier breakdown.           "statement": "Let $d\\ge1$, let $C\\subseteq\\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $P_C(y)$ be the unique nearest point in $C$ to $y$, whose existence and uniqueness are [[thm-nearest-point-in-a-nonempty-closed-convex-set]]. For $x\\in C$, set\n$$N_C(x)=\\{n\\in\\mathbb R^d:\\langle n,z-x\\rangle\\le0\\text{ for every }z\\in C\\};$$\nfor $x\\notin C$, set $N_C(x)=\\varnothing$. On $C$ this is the outward normal cone of [[def-kkt-residual-and-normal-cone]]. The projection variational inequality of [[lem-projection-onto-a-closed-convex-set-has-the-variational-inequality]] says $P_C(y)=p$ exactly when $p\\in C$ and $y-p\\in N_C(p)$.\n\nFor $T>0$, a solution of the projected contact dynamics with forcing $f:[0,T]\\times C\\to\\mathbb R^d$ and initial state $x_0\\in C$ is an absolutely continuous map $x:[0,T]\\to C$ satisfying\n$$f(t,x(t))-\\dot x(t)\\in N_C(x(t))\\quad\\text{for almost every }t\\in[0,T].$$\nEquivalently, $\\dot x(t)+N_C(x(t))\\ni f(t,x(t))$. For an integer $N\\ge1$, put $h=T/N$, $t_k=kh$, and define the exact explicit projection Euler nodes by\n$$x_{k+1}=P_C\\bigl(x_k+h f(t_k,x_k)\\bigr),\\qquad k=0,\\ldots,N-1,$$\nstarting from $x_0$. Its affine interpolant joins consecutive nodes linearly on each interval $[t_k,t_{k+1}]$.\n\nFor a map $x:[0,T]\\to\\mathbb R^d$, **absolutely continuous** means that each coordinate is absolutely continuous in the scalar sense of [[def-absolutely-continuous-function]], and $\\dot x(t)$ is the vector of coordinate derivatives, from [[def-derivative]], wherever they all exist. The solution condition requires a Lebesgue-null set $N\\subseteq[0,T]$ such that for every $t\\notin N$ all coordinate derivatives exist and the displayed inclusion holds. Here **almost every $t$** is relative to Lebesgue measure $\\lambda$ from [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]], with the convention of [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]].\n"

          "statement": "Let $d\\ge1$, $Q\\subseteq\\mathbb R^d$ be open, $V\\in C^3(Q)$, and $M$ symmetric positive definite. Write $\\Psi_h^E$ and $\\Psi_h^V$ for their admitted one-step maps and $\\varphi_h$ for the exact flow. For sufficiently small $h$, constants $C_E,C_V,L$ independent of $h,N,n$ satisfy\n$$\\|\\Psi_h^E(z)-\\varphi_h(z)\\|\\le C_Eh^2,\\qquad \\|\\Psi_h^V(z)-\\varphi_h(z)\\|\\le C_Vh^3$$\nfor admitted $z\\in K$, and whenever $nh\\le T$,\n$$e_n^E\\le e^{LT}e_0+C_ETe^{LT}h,\\qquad e_n^V\\le e^{LT}e_0+C_VTe^{LT}h^2.$$\nThus symplectic Euler has global order one and leapfrog has global order two on the stated controlled tube.           "statement": "Let $n\\ge1$, let $B\\in\\mathbb R^{n\\times n}$ be symmetric, let $g\\in\\mathbb R^n$, and\nlet $\\Delta>0$. A global minimizer always exists.\n\nThe singular hard case is included as follows. Let $\\mu$ be the least\neigenvalue of $B$ and $E_\\mu$ its eigenspace. If $\\mu<0$, $g\\perp E_\\mu$,\nand the solution $p_0$ of\n$(B-\\mu I)p_0=-g$, $p_0\\perp E_\\mu$, has $\\|p_0\\|_2\\le\\Delta$, then\n$$p_*=p_0+z,\\qquad z\\in E_\\mu,\\qquad \\|z\\|_2^2=\\Delta^2-\\|p_0\\|_2^2$$\nis a global minimizer with the singular multiplier $\\lambda=-\\mu$. If\n$\\|p_0\\|_2<\\Delta$, both signs of any chosen nonzero $z$ of the required\nlength give distinct minimizers.\n\n",

          "title": "The actual-to-predicted ratio approaches one at small radii away from stationarity",
          "statement": "Let $m$ be the model of\n[[def-trust-region-quadratic-model-and-ratio]], with $g\\ne0$, symmetric\n$B$, and radius $\\Delta>0$. Interpret\n$\\|g\\|_2/(2M_B)=+\\infty$ if $M_B=0$, and assume\n$\\Delta\\le\\|g\\|_2/(2M_B)$. Then the predicted reduction is positive and\n$$|\\rho(p)-1|\\le\\frac{2(L+M_B)\\Delta}{\\theta\\|g\\|_2}.$$\nConsequently, for $0<\\eta_2<1$, if $L+M_B>0$ and\n$$\\Delta\\le\\frac{\\theta(1-\\eta_2)\\|g\\|_2}{2(L+M_B)},$$\nthen $\\rho(p)\\ge\\eta_2$. If $L+M_B=0$, then $\\rho(p)=1$.\n\n",

At every iteration let $B_k$\nbe symmetric with $\\|B_k\\|_2\\le M_B$ for a fixed $M_B\\ge0$. Fix\n$0<\\eta_1<\\eta_2<1$, $0<\\gamma_{dec}<1<\\gamma_{inc}$, $0<\\theta_C\\le1$,\nand $0<\\Delta_0\\le\\Delta_{max}$. Start from any $x_0\\in\\mathbb R^n$ and\nconsider an infinite-horizon trajectory that at each nonstationary iteration\nfollows the model-formation, step-selection, ratio, and radius-update rules of\n[[alg-trust-region-method]], with target $0$ and its finite outer-cap return\nomitted.           "statement": "For every nonstationary trial of [[alg-trust-region-method]], the selected\npredicted reduction is positive, and every accepted trial strictly decreases\nthe objective.\n\nAssume the hypotheses and parameter ranges of\n[[thm-trust-region-global-liminf-gradient]], and let $f_{inf}$ be a lower\nbound for $f$. Define\n$$c_\\delta:=\\min\\left\\{\\frac1{2M_B}, \\frac{\\theta_C(1-\\eta_2)}{2(L+M_B)}\\right\\},\\qquad c_R:=\\min\\{\\Delta_0,\\gamma_{dec}\\min\\{c_\\delta,\\Delta_{max}\\}\\},$$\nwhere a zero denominator means $+\\infty$, and put\n$$c_P:=\\min\\{c_R,1/M_B\\},\\qquad c_S:=\\tfrac12\\eta_1\\theta_Cc_P>0.$$\nThen the number $N_s$ of accepted steps before reaching the target and the\nnumber $N_u$ of rejected trials obey\n$$N_s\\le\\frac{f(x_0)-f_{inf}}{c_S\\varepsilon^2},$$\n$$N_u\\le\\frac{\\log(\\Delta_0/r_\\varepsilon)+N_s\\log\\gamma_{inc}} {|\\log\\gamma_{dec}|},\\qquad r_\\varepsilon:=\\min\\{\\Delta_0,\\gamma_{dec}\\min\\{c_\\delta\\varepsilon, \\Delta_{max}\\}\\}.$$\nHere $\\log$ denotes the natural logarithm of a positive real.\nConsequently, accepted steps and total trials $N_s+N_u$ are\n$O(\\varepsilon^{-2})$ as $\\varepsilon\\downarrow0$.           "title": "Adaptive cubic regularization reaches first-order accuracy in O(ε⁻³ᐟ²) evaluations",
          "statement": "Let $n\\ge1$, and let $f:\\mathbb R^n\\to\\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ and bounded\nbelow by $f_{inf}$.\nRun [[alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization]] with exact Hessians and parameters\n$0<\\eta_1<\\eta_2<1$, $\\gamma_{up}>1$, $0<\\gamma_{down}<1$,\n$0<\\kappa<1$, $0<\\kappa_\\theta<1$, and\n$0<\\sigma_{min}\\le\\sigma_k\\le\\sigma_{max}$ with $\\sigma_{max}\\ge3L$.\nSuppose the Hessian is $L$-Lipschitz on every trial segment, and let\n$0<\\varepsilon\\le1$. Let $R\\in\\mathbb N_0$ satisfy\n$\\gamma_{up}^R\\sigma_{min}\\ge3L$ (take $R=0$ if\n$\\sigma_{min}\\ge3L$).\n\nFor the counts below, use the trajectory that follows the trial,\nacceptance/rejection, and regularization-update rules of\n[[alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization]] with its finite outer-cap return\nomitted. The finite-cap conclusion then reinstates that return.\n\nThe algorithm has two complexity guarantees.\n\n1. **Exact model minimizers.** If every solver call returns an exact global\n   minimizer, define\n   $$C_g:=\\sigma_{max}+\\sqrt n\\,L,\\qquad c_g:=\\frac{\\eta_1\\sigma_{min}}{6C_g^{3/2}}.$$\n   Through the first iterate with gradient norm at most $\\varepsilon$, the\n   numbers $N_s$ of accepted steps and $N_u$ of rejected trials satisfy\n   $$N_s\\le [f(x_0)-f_{inf}]c_g^{-1}\\varepsilon^{-3/2}+1,\\qquad N_u\\le R N_s.$$\n\n2. **Admissible inexact model steps.** Suppose each solver-success candidate\n   passes the cubic solution, residual, and Cauchy-decrease checks in\n   [[alg-adaptive-cubic-regularization]], and $\\nabla f$ is $K$-Lipschitz\n   on every trial segment. If the solver succeeds at every nonterminal\n   trial, define\n   $$D_g:=\\frac{\\sigma_{max}+\\sqrt n\\,L+\\kappa_\\theta K} {1-\\kappa_\\theta},\\qquad c_a:=\\frac{\\eta_1\\sigma_{min}}{6D_g^{3/2}}.$$\n   Then the same counts satisfy\n   $$N_s\\le [f(x_0)-f_{inf}]c_a^{-1}\\varepsilon^{-3/2}+1,\\qquad N_u\\le R N_s.$$\n\nIn either case the uncapped process reaches a stationary or target-achieved\niterate with gradient norm at most $\\varepsilon$. For the finite-cap\nalgorithm, an outer cap at least\n$$(R+1)\\left(\\frac{f(x_0)-f_{inf}}{c\\,\\varepsilon^{3/2}}+1\\right)$$\nsuffices, where $c=c_g$ in case 1 and $c=c_a$ in case 2. The resulting\nnumber of outer trials, and their function, gradient, and Hessian evaluation\ncounts, are $O(\\varepsilon^{-3/2})$. These counts do not bound the internal\nwork of the model solver.\n\n",

          "statement": "Input a finite horizon $T>0$, a time step $\\Delta t>0$, an age cutoff $A>0$, bounded nonnegative rates $\\mu,\\beta$ on $[0,A]$, and a finite positive initial quadrature $(a_i,m_i^0)_{i=1}^I$ supported in $[0,A)$ for the initial age measure on that interval. One option, when a nonnegative real-valued initial density $n_0$ is evaluable at every point of $[0,A]$, is to choose any finite partition $0=b_0<\\cdots<b_I=A$ and apply [[alg-composite-midpoint-rule]] with $n=1$ separately on each cell $[b_{i-1},b_i]$: set $\\Delta a_i=b_i-b_{i-1}$, $a_i=(b_{i-1}+b_i)/2$, and $m_i^0=Q_M(n_0;b_{i-1},b_i,1)=\\Delta a_i\\,n_0(a_i)$ for $1\\le i\\le I$.           "statement": "Let $q(p)=c^Tp+\\tfrac12p^TBp$ on $\\mathbb R^n$, where $B=B^T$ is positive\ndefinite. Let the feasible set be the nonempty polyhedron\n$$C=\\{p:Ap=b,\\ G_ip+d_i\\le0\\ (1\\le i\\le m)\\},$$\nwhere the equality rows of $A$ are linearly independent (zero rows are\nallowed). Then $q$ has a unique minimizer $p_*$. There are equality\nmultipliers $\\nu$ and inequality multipliers $\\lambda_i\\ge0$ such that\n$$Bp_*+c+A^T\\nu+\\sum_i\\lambda_iG_i^T=0, \\qquad \\lambda_i(G_ip_*+d_i)=0.$$\nThey can be chosen so that the equality rows and the active inequality rows\nwith $\\lambda_i>0$ are linearly independent. This KKT tuple certifies the\nglobal minimizer.\n\n"
        },

          "id": "alg-sqp-exhaustive-active-set-qp-solve",

            "lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature"

          "dependency_level": 3,
          "justified_by": [
            "thm-sqp-exhaustive-active-set-qp-solve-correct-finite"
          ],
          "statement": "Input an SQP subproblem from [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]],\nusing exact real arithmetic. Let $q$ and $m$ be the numbers of equality and\ninequality constraints. Put $A^{\\rm eq}=Dh(x)$, $b^{\\rm eq}=-h(x)$,\n$G=Dg(x)$, $d=g(x)$, and $c=\\nabla f(x)$, so $G_i=Dg_i(x)$ and\n$d_i=g_i(x)$ for $1\\le i\\le m$. First reduce the linearized equality system\n$A^{\\rm eq}p=b^{\\rm eq}$: test consistency, and, if consistent, retain the\nlexicographically first maximal independent set $E\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,q\\}$\nof equality row indices with their right-hand sides. If it is inconsistent,\nreturn `QP-infeasible`. Within each retained row set, use increasing original\nindices; an empty row set contributes no rows or right-hand-side entries.\n\nFor each subset $J\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,m\\}$ in increasing bit-mask order:\n\n1. Stack the equality rows $(A^{\\rm eq})_E$ and the inequality rows $G_J$,\n   in that order. If these rows are dependent, skip $J$.\n2. Treat the selected inequalities as equalities $G_ip=-d_i$ and solve\n   $$\\begin{bmatrix}B&A_J^T\\\\A_J&0\\end{bmatrix} \\binom{p}{\\eta}=\\binom{-c}{b_J},$$\n   where $A_J=\\binom{(A^{\\rm eq})_E}{G_J}$ and\n   $b_J=\\binom{(b^{\\rm eq})_E}{-d_J}$. Thus the equality entries of $b_J$\n   are $-h_a(x)$ for $a\\in E$, followed by $-g_i(x)$ for $i\\in J$,\n   in the declared row order. The multiplier vector $\\eta$ is stored in this\n   same order. The KKT matrix is\n   nonsingular by [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]].\n3. Discard the candidate if any linearized inequality is violated or any\n   selected inequality multiplier is negative. Otherwise store $(p,\\eta,J)$.\n\nIf no candidate is stored, return `QP-infeasible`.           "deps": [

          "strategy": "1.1 At $x=(c,s)$, $h(x)=0$, $Dh(x)=2(c,s)$, and $\\nabla f(x)=4(c,s)-(1,0)$. The unit tangent $t=(-s,c)$ satisfies $t^T\\nabla f(x)=s$. The QP constraint gives $p\\in\\operatorname{span}(t)$; minimizing $\\nabla f(x)^Tp+\\tfrac12\\|p\\|_2^2$ on this line gives $p=-st=(s^2,-sc)$. Its QP multiplier is $-(4-c)/2$, since $p+\\nabla f(x)=(4-c)(c,s)$. [given, F1, A1, algebra]\n\n1.2 Here $Dh(x)Dh(x)^T=4$, so [F3] gives $w=(-cs^2/2,-s^3/2)$ and $\\|w\\|_2=s^2/2$. Direct substitution into the quadratic constraint yields $$h(x+p+w)=\\frac{s^4}{4}.$$ The corrected first coordinate is $c+s^2(1-c/2)$, so the corrected objective change is $-s^2(1-c/2)+s^4/2$. Adding the penalty contribution gives $$\\psi_\\rho(x+p+w)-\\psi_\\rho(x) =-s^2(1-c/2)+s^4(1/2+\\rho/4).$$ [A1, F3, algebra]\n\n2.1 Since $x^Tp=0$ and $\\|p\\|_2^2=s^2$, $h(x+p)=s^2$. Also $\\nabla f(x)^Tp=-s^2$, so [F2] gives $D_\\rho=s^2$. The objective changes by $s^2$, while the equality violation changes from zero to $s^2$; hence the full-step merit change is $(1+\\rho)s^2>0$, which fails the Armijo right side $-\\sigma s^2<0$. [A1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]\n\n3.1 Divide the corrected merit change plus $\\sigma D_\\rho$ by $s^2$. With $\\sigma=1/4$, the result is $-1+c/2+s^2(1/2+\\rho/4)+1/4$, which tends to $-1/4$ as $\\theta\\to0$. It is therefore negative for all sufficiently small nonzero $\\theta$, proving the SOC Armijo test passes. The explicit $O(s^2)$ correction norm and $O(s^4)$ residual satisfy the quadratic-size and cubic-residual bounds of [F4]. [A1, F4, F5, step 1.2, algebra] ∎"

          "statement": "Input: an open domain $U$, a Hermitian response matrix map $F:U\\to\\mathbb H_n$,\nand its gapped occupied-projector map $\\Phi$ from\n[[def-self-consistent-projector-response-map]]; a nonempty complete invariant\nset $K\\subseteq U\\cap\\mathcal P_r$ with $\\Phi(K)\\subseteq K$ and certified\ncontraction factor $0\\le q<1$; an initial projector $P_0\\in K$; a certified\ninitial error bound $E_0\\ge\\|P_0-P_*\\|_F$ for the unique fixed point $P_*$;\nresidual tolerance $\\varepsilon\\ge0$; finite update budget $N\\in\\mathbb N_0$;\nmemory $m\\ge1$; coefficient cap $C\\ge1$; a Hermitian eigensolver that, for a\nmatrix $M$, returns a certified ordered spectrum and occupied projector when\nthe $r$th gap is strict, a certified no-gap result, or a failure to certify the\nspectrum; an approximate response evaluator that at $X\\in K$ returns\n$\\widetilde\\Phi(X)\\in K$ and $\\eta(X)\\ge0$ with\n$\\|\\widetilde\\Phi(X)-\\Phi(X)\\|_F\\le\\eta(X)$, or a failure status; and a\nconstrained least-squares solver that either returns the certified global\nminimizer with the minimum-norm tie-break for the residuals and cap $C$, or\nreports failure. Every called solver returns one of its specified results.\n\nThe terminal output is $(P_k,\\texttt{status},b,k)$, where $P_k$ is the current\nprojector and $b$ is its certified error bound. The current budget $E_k$\nremains valid at gap, eigensolver, response-evaluation, or invariance-certificate\nfailure statuses.\n\nFor $k=0,\\ldots,N$:\n\n1. If no certified response evaluation is cached for $P_k$, compute $F(P_k)$ and call the eigensolver on it. If the eigensolver certifies no strict gap, return $(P_k,\\texttt{gap-loss},E_k,k)$; if it fails to certify the spectrum, return $(P_k,\\texttt{eigensolve-failure},E_k,k)$. With a certified strict gap, call the approximate response evaluator. If it fails, return $(P_k,\\texttt{response-evaluation-failure},E_k,k)$. Cache $(F(P_k),\\widetilde\\Phi(P_k),\\eta(P_k))$ at exactly $P_k$. Whether this evaluation is new or cached, check that the certified baseline output belongs to $K$; if not, return $(P_k,\\texttt{invariance-certificate-failure},E_k,k)$. Retain the current pair $(P_k,F(P_k))$ for this proposal step. Set $\\bar\\rho_k=\\|P_k-\\widetilde\\Phi(P_k)\\|_F+\\eta(P_k)$. If $\\bar\\rho_k\\le\\varepsilon$, return $(P_k,\\texttt{residual-tolerance-met},\\bar\\rho_k/(1-q),k)$.\n2. If $k=N$, return $(P_k,\\texttt{iteration-budget-exhausted},E_k,k)$.\n3.           "dependency_level": 1,
          "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. For $\\Omega=(0,1)$, realize $V=H^1(0,1)$ by its unique absolutely continuous representatives, with norm $\\|v\\|_V=(\\|v\\|_2^2+\\|v'\\|_2^2)^{1/2}$. For a smooth state satisfying $-u''+u=f$, $u'(0)=0$, and $u'(1)=g$, integration by parts gives the weak boundary load $v\\mapsto g v(1)$. The boundary control parameter is a scalar, equivalently $L^2(\\{1\\})$ for counting measure. For $g\\ne0$, its trace functional is not representable by an interior density $q\\in L^2(0,1)$; for $g=0$, both loads include the zero functional. Thus the boundary control space and its trace operator must be specified separately from the distributed-control space $L^2(0,1)$.\n\n"

          "id": "def-hybrid-mode-guard-reset-system",
          "kind": "definition",
          "title": "Smooth hybrid ODE modes, guards, resets, and deterministic event priority",
          "deps": [
            "def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution",
            "def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse"
          ],
          "dependency_level": 0,
          "statement": "A **smooth hybrid ODE system** on a finite horizon $[0,T]$, with $T\\ge0$ and positive integer state dimension $d\\ge1$, consists of a finite mode set $M$, an open state-time domain $D_m\\subseteq\\mathbb R\\times\\mathbb R^d$ and a $C^1$ vector field $f_m:D_m\\to\\mathbb R^d$ for each $m\\in M$, a finite set of directed transitions $(m,n)$, and for each transition a $C^1$ scalar guard $g_{mn}:D_m\\to\\mathbb R$, a declared crossing orientation $\\sigma_{mn}\\in\\{-1,+1\\}$, and a $C^1$ reset map $R_{mn}:U_{mn}\\to\\mathbb R^d$ on an open neighborhood $U_{mn}\\subseteq D_m$ of the guard zero set, satisfying $(t,R_{mn}(t,x))\\in D_n$ for every $(t,x)\\in U_{mn}$. Here $C^1$ has the meaning in [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]. In mode $m$, a trajectory is a solution of the first-order initial-value problem $y'=f_m(t,y)$ in the sense of [[def-first-order-ode-initial-value-problem-and-solution]]. It follows that mode only until the selected event time.\n\nAn **event time** for transition $(m,n)$ is a time $\\tau$ at which $g_{mn}(\\tau,y(\\tau))=0$ and the guard crosses in its declared direction, meaning $\\sigma_{mn}\\frac{d}{dt}g_{mn}(t,y(t))|_{t=\\tau}>0$. It is **transverse** with margin $\\nu>0$ on a bracket when $\\sigma_{mn}\\frac{d}{dt}g_{mn}(t,y(t))\\ge\\nu$ throughout that bracket. At an event, the state changes from $y(\\tau^-)$ to $R_{mn}(\\tau,y(\\tau^-))$ and the mode changes from $m$ to $n$. A **deterministic event-priority rule** is a fixed total order on the finite outgoing transition set of each mode; if several enabled guards vanish at exactly the same first time, the least transition in that order is selected.\n\nA hybrid trajectory has a **finite separated event list** on $[0,T]$ when it has finitely many event times $0<\\tau_1<\\cdots<\\tau_N<T$ and some $\\delta>0$ with $\\tau_{j+1}-\\tau_j\\ge\\delta$ for each adjacent pair. The definition does not assert that a solution exists, that an event is detected, or that the event list is finite. Those are separate hypotheses or conclusions.\n"
